newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria awards contracts to boost air safety.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria awards contracts to boost air safety.

text.p: Nigeria, hit by a series of air disasters, said on Wednesday it had awarded a $23 million contract to the French group Alcatel Alsthom to install modern instrument landing systems at its 19 airports.
"The contract is part of our efforts to make our airspace safer," Aviation Minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh told Reuters in the capital Abuja.
"In addition, we have also awarded a contract for the survey of our entire airspace for radar coverage, which again is to ensure safety of our airspace," he said.
Nigeria has in recent years suffered a series of air disasters, the worst being the crash of a passenger jet into a lagoon near Lagos last November killing all 143 people on board.
Udo-Imeh said the West African nation had been shaken by the spate of air crashes and was yet to recover from them.
"But with the renewed effort to make our airspace safer if there is any disaster we'll know it is an act of God, the human lapses having being taken care of," he added.
He said human errors in the running of the aviation industry had also been identified.
"This is why we have planned to computerise the operations at the airport and also to install satellite systems," he added.

Alcatel has one year to complete the job of installing the instrument landing systems and has already started making them to Nigeria's specification, the minister said. The contract was worth $23 million, he added.
Economic hardships for Africa's most populous nation have affected the aviation industry like everything else in the country.
Local airlines recently won government approval to double domestic air fares after more than two years of demanding an increase in order to stay afloat.
Udo-Imeh said the increase was necessary in order for the airlines to make enough money to ensure safety of aircraft.
"The last time the government approved increase in airfares was in 1994 and since then the exchange rate has deteriorated while their maintenance costs have gone up," he said.
Foreign airlines operating international flights are allowed to quote their fares in dollars and then convert to the local currency at the market rate.
The minister said an Africa-Indian Ocean air navigation conference opening in Abuja next Monday would consider how to improve air safety in Africa.
